findings: Written: T2 dual holds whenever A or B is normal. This follows from a new lemma: any 2D range with a <=2-dim leg satisfies ||XP_F||^2<=||X||^2/2, by the v2 ladder plus the range-wise dual converse.
Written, conditional on the named Boettcher-Wenzel import: T2 holds for B=-A^T.
Exact integer descent search (24 starts x 600 iterations): no counterexample; every run ends with q2>0 and ratio <1e-10. The limit points sit in the qubit corner, where all legs are effectively 2D.
Exact Hessian at the cross-sector equality point X0=|0><1|(x)I+I(x)|0><1|: negative semidefinite, inertia (0,34,26). Overestimating faults make it indefinite.
exact_gap: T2 remains unproved when both top-2 singular spaces of X have all legs >=3 and are not spread, i.e. Z2. Possible literature coincidence is an unverified recollection and is not used as a premise.
next_action: Attempt to extend the supported-leg lemma to block-reducible B (2+2 reducing subspaces) or to rank-one A, or a second-order test at further equality points. No held input; f153/f62 unchanged.
